content: F1 Live Timing REST API (f1-livetiming-api) Host your own high-performance, real-time REST API server for Formula 1 live timing, driver standings, tyre strategies, and race control telemetry. Connected directly to the official F1 SignalR Core streaming endpoint (livetiming.formula1.com). --- Core Architecture & Data Principles Designed for absolute data fidelity and zero-latency local consumption, f1-livetiming-api is built on three pillars: 1. Zero Field Renaming (1:1 PascalCase Fidelity) : Every telemetry property emitted by Formula 1 SignalR servers is preserved verbatim in its native PascalCase convention (Position, GapToLeader, BestLapTime, TeamColour, Stints, etc.). No artificial camelCase transformations or hardcoded driver dictionaries are used; driver identities are natively sourced from the official DriverList stream. 1. Background Delta-Merge Synchronisation : F1 SignalR operates via a delta protocol (transmitting only modified properties per tick). The server maintains an in-memory state store powered by a custom deep-merge engine (src/utils/merge.js). Incoming deltas are seamlessly merged into server RAM in the background without overwriting adjacent objects or arrays. 1. Zero Outbound HTTP Overhead (100% Local Reads) : When your dashboard, frontend, or script queries any endpoint on this server, zero requests are dispatched to Formula 1 servers . All REST responses read straight from local memory in sub-millisecond time. You can poll the local endpoints at 1,000 requests per second with zero risk of rate-limiting or IP bans . --- Specialized & Decoupled REST Endpoints To avoid monolithic responses and enable clean modular frontend designs, telemetry feeds are separated into distinct, targeted domain endpoints. All endpoints default to port 3000 (override via PORT environment variable) with standard JSON format and CORS enabled. Driver Standings & Leaderboards Method Endpoint Alias Description ------- ---------------------- ----- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- GET /api/standings - Dedicated driver classification sorted by live Position. Combines driver identity and timing intervals (GapToLeader, BestLapTime, Sectors, Speeds) without tyre stint arrays or meeting overhead. GET /api/standings/:id - Retrieves live timing and rank for a specific driver by their racing number (e.g., /api/standings/1 or /api/standings/44). GET /api/leaderboard - All-in-one comprehensive view combining driver metadata, live gaps, tyre stints, current lap count, and session meeting data into a single unified response. GET /api/leaderboard/:id - Comprehensive unified telemetry package for an individual driver. Tyre Strategies & Stint Chronology Method Endpoint Alias Description ------- ---------------- ----------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- GET /api/tyres /api/stints Decoupled tyre strategy feed. Exposes compounds (SOFT, MEDIUM, HARD, INTERMEDIATE, WET), total lap wear per set, grid vs current line positions, enriched with driver acronyms and team hex colors. GET /api/tyres/:id /api/stints/:id Detailed stint chronology and active compound allocation for a specific driver. Driver Directory & Meeting Metadata Method Endpoint Description ------- ------------------ ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- GET /api/drivers Official meeting driver roster (DriverList), providing full names, broadcasting acronyms (Tla), team names, hex RGB team colors, country codes, and headshot references. GET /api/drivers/:id Specific team and personal metadata for a designated racing number. Track Status, Weather & Race Control Method Endpoint Alias Description ------- ------------------- ----------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- GET /api/session - Current meeting identifier, official session name, session type (Practice, Qualifying, Race, Sprint), and lifecycle status. GET /api/lap-count /api/laps Live lap counter and scheduled total meeting laps ({ "CurrentLap": 24, "TotalLaps": 57 }). GET /api/weather - Real-time meteorological telemetry: Air temperature, track surface temperature, relative humidity, wind speed/direction, and rain detection sensors. GET /api/race-control /api/flags Official FIA Race Control broadcasts: Track flag statuses (GREEN, YELLOW, RED), safety car deployments (SC, VSC), DRS enablement, and penalty warnings. GET /api/radio /api/team-radio Recent team radio broadcast audio capture notifications, enriched with driver and team identity. Server Health Diagnostics Method Endpoint Description ------- ------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- GET /api/status Real-time diagnostics detailing WebSocket connectivity state (CONNECTED / DISCONNECTED), server process uptime in seconds, and timestamp of the last received SignalR transmission. --- Session Schema Variations (Practice vs Race) Because F1 SignalR adjusts its broadcast payload according to session discipline, the schema-agnostic deep merge natively reflects these variations across the API: Race & Sprint Sessions Focus is placed on track positioning, intervals, and pit lane activity: - Position : Live numeric racing position used for automatic leaderboard ranking. - GapToLeader : Object detailing gap to P1 (e.g., {"Value": "+4.128", "Catching": false} or {"Value": "LEADER"}). - IntervalToPositionAhead : Distance interval to the immediate preceding driver. - InPit / PitOut : Live boolean indicators of pit lane transit. - NumberOfPitStops : Official count of completed box stops. - Retired / Stopped : DNF status flags, automatically shifting retired cars to the classification tail during dynamic sorting. Practice, Qualifying & Shootout Sessions Focus shifts to timed lap speed, sector accuracy, and qualification drop zone thresholds: - BestLapTime : Current session personal benchmark ({"Value": "1:28.914", "PersonalFastest": true, "OverallFastest": true}). - BestLapTimes : Dictionary separating fastest laps by qualification segment (key "0" for Q1, "1" for Q2, "2" for Q3). - Stats : Qualifying gap statistics including time variance to session leader (TimeDiffToFastest) and immediate ranking predecessor (TimeDifftoPositionAhead). - Sectors / Speeds : Sector performance blocks and speed trap recordings at the Finish Line (FL), maximum Speed Trap (ST), and intermediate sectors (I1, I2). --- Installation & Server Startup Prerequisites Requires Node.js (v18 or newer recommended for native fetch support during HTTP SignalR negotiation). Running the Server Upon initialization, the server will display its routing manifest and initiate F1 SignalR Core connection sequences: --- Quick Usage Examples (cURL & JSON) 1. Fetch Dedicated Driver Standings (/api/standings) Returns clean driver classification sorted by live position, stripped of heavy tyre stint histories. Example JSON Response: --- 2. Fetch Tyre Strategies & Stints (/api/tyres or /api/stints) Ideal for strategic dashboards tracking tyre degradation and compound allocations. Example JSON Response: --- 3. Fetch Real-Time Meteorological Telemetry (/api/weather) Retrieves atmospheric sensors directly from trackside F1 instrumentation. Example JSON Response: --- 4. Monitor Server & WebSocket Health (/api/status) Used by uptime monitors or UI polling guards to verify active live timing stream health. Example JSON Response: --- Source Directory Overview

Enriched with driver TLA, TeamColour, and BroadcastName without altering native PascalCase SignalR properties. Main entry point for the F1 Live Timing REST API Server. Connects to Formula 1 SignalR Core live telemetry and exposes modular REST endpoints. Service responsible for assembling live telemetry, driver standings, tyre strategies, and session diagnostics directly from SignalR Core raw data streams without altering field names or case (PascalCase preserved). Utility for deeply merging F1 SignalR Core delta payloads into an existing state tree. F1 SignalR uses a delta protocol where only changed fields in channels like TimingData or TimingAppData are sent in each message. Deep merging ensures that nested structures (such as Sectors, Speeds, or Stints) are cleanly updated without overwriting existing sibling fields.
